items.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Yeah. I met Trane. Right here.

ctx.x: Yes. I just saw him. We just – I don’t think – do I have it with me? We just contributed to this book on John Coltrane. T. J. wrote the forward. I contributed one chapter. Actually, then I interviewed Ollie Wilson for it. T. J. wrote the forward for that.

items.title: Ellis Marsalis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 7, 2020
items.q: it took me back to Elvin and Trane, because I mean it was memorable you know because I mean it was like fire.

ctx.x: All right. How about the best gig you ever played?

I don’t know. Let’s see. I think the most interesting job that I have ever played, it was really at the Kennedy Center and there was like a trad gig. I was playing piano and Louis Barbarin was playing drums, Louis Cottrell was playing clarinet, Alvin Alcorn was playing trumpet and Waldren Joseph was playing trombone. And we were doing like “Sensation Rag” — the traditional music. And it was the first time that I can remember being able to really play on a good piano with the older guys.
